title: terraform: refactor private GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking and state layout
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated ad-hoc node pool, IAM and networking modules. This caused duplication, inconsistent tagging and a brittle state layout that made upgrades and multi-cluster installs error-prone. This PR introduces a unified GPU node-pool module, centralized IAM roles for private installs, normalized VPC/subnet layout and a new state backend layout + migration tooling.

Summary: single-module API for GPU node pools (supports gke/eks/aks flavors via vars), dedicated IAM module with least-privilege roles for node-pool and control-plane components, network module that produces deterministic subnet ranges and tags, and a documented state layout change with a helper migration script to move remote state paths without resource re-creation.

Checklist:
- [x] Refactor gpu-node-pool module to accept instance_type/accelerator/taints/max_pods
- [x] Add iam/roles module + automated tests for policy boundaries
- [x] Normalize network module outputs (subnet_ids, route_table_ids) and tagging 
- [x] Add modules/state/backend.tf and modules/state/README.md documenting migration steps
- [x] Add scripts/tfstate-migrate.py (dry-run and apply modes)
- [x] Update examples/private-deploy to new module interface and include rolling upgrade guidance
- [x] CI: terraform fmt/validate and module unit tests

Migration notes (high level): changing state layout is a breaking operation for managed backends. There is an automated helper (scripts/tfstate-migrate.py) that performs a safe, idempotent move of state keys from the legacy layout to the new one. The README in modules/state contains a step-by-step migration checklist (snapshot backend, dry-run, run migration, validate in staging). Backends supported: S3-compatible, GCS and Azure Blob. The modules retain compatibility shims for legacy variable names for one release cycle to ease rollouts.

Testing: validated terraform fmt/validate in CI, added terratest unit tests for node-pool and iam modules, and ran a full integration smoke deploy in staging against a small dedicated GPU cluster. Performed a dry-run migration and verified state mapping.

Impact: Operators with existing private deployments must schedule a migration window. The migration is non-destructive but requires backend access and locking permissions. See modules/state/README.md for details and team migration runbook.

Detailed changes are summarized below.

review_comments: Priya: left nits on variable naming and suggested breaking module outputs for multi-region. Author: addressed nits, added outputs for region-scoped subnet_ids and documented decision in README.

Carlos: flagged IAM scope for node pool service account being too permissive. Author: tightened policy to principle-of-least-privilege and added unit test that asserts denied actions.

Liam: asked about rolling upgrade strategy for node pools to avoid capacity loss. Author: documented recommended sequence (create new pool -> cordon/drain -> scale down old pool) and added example in examples/private-deploy/README.md.

merge_details: Merged via squash on 2026-03-01 by Maya Patel. Squash commit message consolidates refactor and migration helper notes. Merge included updated release notes and modules/state/README.md.
release_notes:
- Refactor private Terraform: unified GPU node pool module and centralized IAM roles.
- Normalize networking module outputs and tags for predictable private installs.
- New state layout and migration tooling (scripts/tfstate-migrate.py).
- Operators must follow migration steps in modules/state/README.md before upgrading the module version.
migration_notes: See modules/state/README.md for full migration steps. High level: 1) run scripts/tfstate-migrate.py --dry-run against current remote state 2) take snapshot of remote backend 3) run migration with --apply (ensure backend lock) 4) validate resources in staging 5) apply to production during maintenance window. Script supports S3/GCS/Azure and outputs mapping between old and new keys.

- integration smoke deploy on a small dedicated GPU cluster in staging
- end-to-end private deploy using updated examples with tfstate migration dry-run
notes: Coordinate upgrade date with platform and affected customers. For self-managed backends, provide the migration script and runbook. Compatibility: legacy variable names are accepted for one release cycle as a shim.
